key_insight: ReScene4D formalizes and solves temporally sparse 4D semantic instance segmentation: maintaining consistent instance identities across intermittently captured indoor 3D scans even when objects move, appear, or disappear between observations.
problem_solved: Existing 3D semantic instance segmentation methods assume dense, continuous observations and fail to preserve instance identity across sparse, time-separated scans where changes are unobserved. This work addresses the challenge of jointly segmenting, identifying, and temporally associating object instances in evolving indoor scenes.
method: Define the temporally sparse 4D SIS task and evaluation protocol to measure segmentation, identification, and temporal association under intermittent capture.

Propose a joint pipeline that performs per-scan 3D instance segmentation and links instances across time with a temporal association module that handles object appearance, disappearance, and motion gaps.
Provide an evaluation benchmark (dataset and metrics) and experiments to quantify temporal consistency and instance tracking performance in evolving indoor scenes.
impact: Enables robust scene understanding for applications that rely on intermittent 3D sensing (robotics, AR/VR, long-term mapping), by ensuring object-level consistency over time and making downstream tasks—like tracking, change detection, and semantic mapping—more reliable.

paper_title: ReScene4D: Temporally Consistent Semantic Instance Segmentation of Evolving Indoor 3D Scenes
paper_authors: Emily Steiner, Jianhao Zheng, Henry Howard-Jenkins, Chris Xie, Iro Armeni
